A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, research questions, methods, and substantial retained evidence. Their complete text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-extraction experiments, activation-inversion measurements, PersonaQA experiments, probing results, and prompt-sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional knowledge-mismatch controls, a multiple-output baseline, and entity-resolution experiments.

M1.justification: The underlying LIT, Patchscopes, inversion, and logistic-probing procedures remain unchanged. Different fine-tuned model configurations and entity-resolution prompts extend the experimental investigation without introducing a new verbalization algorithm or training objective.

E1.justification: The original datasets remain, but Appendices I.1 and J extend coverage to entity-resolution tasks. In particular, Appendix J requires identifying an unnamed persona from its attributes, changing both the available input information and the required prediction beyond the earlier attribute-extraction evaluations.

E2.justification: Appendix G.8 adds a zero-shot comparator that combines multiple sampled outputs to emulate Patchscopes evaluation. Section 5.3 also replaces the earlier untrained Patchscopes configuration with one using a fantasy-finetuned verbalizer. The principal comparison methods otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Besides the changed Patchscopes training condition in Section 5.3, v3 introduces matched multiple-output evaluation in G.8. Entity-resolution experiments add corresponding-layer patching, evaluation over layers 1–10 and 20–31, ROUGE-L, and partial versus full name matching. These substantially extend the evaluation design; most original protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New controls test whether verbalizers answer using knowledge absent from the target model (Section 5.4) and whether multiple guessing opportunities explain Patchscopes results (G.8). Appendices I–J add layerwise knowledge-mismatch analyses and report failure without a priming phrase. The original prompt-sensitivity analysis is retained as Appendix H.

E5.justification: Appendix G.8 newly specifies sampling L' zero-shot outputs with different seeds for its control; this is not evidence of additional replicated training runs. Existing significance captions also change 'significantly worse' to 'significantly different,' while retaining McNemar's test, Bonferroni correction, and the reported significance markers.

E6.justification: v1 Table 23 reports zero accuracy for both verbalizers across all six attributes; v3 Table 5 reports 0.18–0.47 for Patchscopes and 0.15–0.33 for LIT, with the probe row unchanged. At least the Patchscopes training condition differs, preventing a same-setting improvement claim. Knowledge-verification values also change in v3 Tables 22–23, and Tables 6, 24, and 30–32 add substantial new results.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs, and the existing mathematical notation and method definitions are retained. The new expressivity and shared-parameter arguments are conceptual interpretations; the additional matching criteria are experimental metrics.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes verbalizer failure even after fantasy training and the superiority of simple probes. v3 instead reports conditional verbalization success when knowledge overlaps, removes that probe-superiority conclusion, and adds the central claim that a more knowledgeable verbalizer can fabricate apparent target-model knowledge. The introduction and conclusion also qualify earlier broad failure claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving multiple-output guessing, excessive verbalizer expressivity, and shared-parameter continuation during entity resolution. It interprets revised Section 5.3 results through knowledge overlap and discusses priming dependence and difficulties attributing partial-name success. A dedicated limitations section makes task, model-size, and inversion-layer restrictions explicit.

D1.justification: New Appendix C summarizes model training and dataset usage, while Appendix D supplies a lower-bound estimate of 2,996.6 combined GPU hours with a task-level breakdown. New experiments document prompts, sampling, and layer choices. Most existing hyperparameters remain unchanged, and the promised code release still uses the same placeholder.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gottesman et al. (2025), Li et al. (2025), and Lin (2004). It also contrasts its expressivity findings with Patchscopes' proposed benefits and relates the new entity-resolution setting to that work. The broader positioning around verbalization and explanation faithfulness remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative sequence and much appendix prose are retained. v3 revises contribution statements, takeaways, and conclusions; standardizes model names; adds a dedicated limitations section; and reorganizes appendix headings around the additional material. These are targeted editorial and structural revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The display substantially expands through new control-result tables, a training inventory, a detailed compute table, and layerwise entity-resolution tables. The revised probing comparison moves from v1 Appendix Table 23 to v3 main Table 5, and the inversion tables exchange order. Figures 2–3 receive small graphical edits; the original sensitivity plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The multiple-output control in G.8 and the knowledge-rich-verbalizer experiment in Section 5.4 better test alternative explanations for apparent interpretability, while narrower claims improve calibration. However, v3 Table 23 still describes zero verbalization despite nonzero results in Table 5, and Appendix I.1 misidentifies a model pairing in Table 30. These reporting inconsistencies limit the net quality gain.
